recognize_zh: 一顆形狀不規則的巨大組織球，細胞核偏在上方、體積小，細胞質豐富淡藍並呈纖細波紋條紋，像揉皺的面紙；和旁邊的小淋巴球相比非常大，符合高雪氏細胞（Gaucher cell）。
features: Large histiocyte with an irregular, elongated outline, several times the size of the adjacent lymphocyte
Single eccentric nucleus at the upper pole with moderately condensed chromatin and no prominent nucleolus
Abundant pale blue cytoplasm with fine wavy fibrillary striations (crumpled tissue paper appearance)
No foamy vacuoles, discrete granules, or ingested cells
Background small lymphocyte, a myeloid cell with an indented nucleus, and red cells with drying artifact
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a large histiocyte with an irregular, elongated outline among small lymphoid and myeloid cells; red cells show refractile drying artifact. The histiocyte has a small eccentric nucleus and abundant pale blue cytoplasm with fine, wavy fibrillary striations imparting a crumpled tissue paper appearance. No foamy vacuolation, ceroid granules, or hemophagocytosis is present. Findings are consistent with a Gaucher cell; confirmation by glucocerebrosidase enzyme assay or GBA1 testing is recommended.

ddx.dx: Pseudo-Gaucher cells (CML, plasma cell myeloma, thalassemia, mycobacterial infection)
ddx.vs: Cannot be separated by morphology alone; the underlying disease, AFB stain, and normal glucocerebrosidase activity distinguish them.
Niemann-Pick cells have finely foamy, bubbly cytoplasm rather than wrinkled fibrillary striations.
Sea-blue histiocytes show discrete blue-green granules instead of a striated cytoplasmic texture.
